bib.title: Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context", Shengnan An, Zexiong Ma, Zeqi Lin, Nanning Zheng, Jian-Guang Lou (Xi'an Jiaotong U., Peking U., Microsoft). The PDF is marked "Preprint", arXiv:2404.16811v2 [cs.CL], 26 Apr 2024. No venue is printed. The work was done during an internship at Microsoft.

COVERAGE: All 62,750 chars read: abstract, body, Tables 1-3, appendices A-D, and references skimmed. Figure data (curves) is not in the extraction, so only the tables and text numbers are available. A grep of the target note 11-failure-modes.md for "lost-in-the-middle" or "lost in the middle" found no match, so I could not see which claims it needs.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- The authors attribute lost-in-the-middle to a position bias in training data. They state this as a hypothesis and do not test it directly.
  number: none
  setup: Argument from pre-training next-token loss and from system-message placement in SFT.
  quote: "We hypothesize that the root cause of lost-in-the-middle stems from the unintentional bias hidden in the general training data."
  where: Intro, p.2
- Definition: models handle the start and end of a long context but miss the middle. The authors cite Liu et al. 2024 and Xu et al. 2023 for this.
  number: none
  setup: Background claim, not measured here.
  quote: "while the LLM can comprehend the information at the beginning and end of the long context, it often overlooks the information in the middle."
  where: Intro, p.2
- Vanilla Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 loses a lot of middle information on all three VAL probes. Its worst-to-best position gap is 47.3 points averaged over the probes (the paper's "AllAvg Gap").
  number: Min-max gap, averaged over the three probes (AllAvg): 47.3 (Mistral-v0.2) vs 13.9 (FILM-7B), 32.1 (GPT-4-Turbo)
  setup: VAL Probing, about 32K-token contexts, about 3K examples per task. Greedy decoding. The Gap is the max minus min performance across positions, so smaller means more position-robust.
  quote: "Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (Jiang et al., 2023) 74.2 32.1 20.3 59.5 47.5 77.0 47.3 56.2" and "FILM-7B (ours) 85.4 6.1 83.3 18.7 89.0 16.8 85.9 13.9"
  where: Table 1, p.6. The column layout is Avg/Gap per task (Document, Code, Database), then All. The "47.3 56.2" ends the Mistral row, so Mistral's All-Avg is 47.3 and its All-Gap is 56.2. See PROBLEMS for how I read the columns.
- Other long-context models still show the middle loss despite near-perfect Needle-in-the-Haystack (NIAH) scores.
  number: AllAvg Gap: LongAlign-7B-64K 36.4, LongAlign-13B-64K 27.1, InternLM2-chat-7B 40.0, InternLM2-chat-20B 43.3, GPT-4-Turbo 32.1, FILM-7B 13.9
  setup: Same as the previous claim.
  quote: "Despite their extended training context windows, these models still encounter the lost-in-the-middle problem. This is particularly noteworthy given their near-perfect performance on the Needle-in-the-Haystack task."
  where: Sec 4.2, p.8, and Table 1
- NIAH overstates long-context ability. It uses document-style text and forward retrieval, which induction heads make easy.
  number: none
  setup: Argument plus the probe results above. The forward-retrieval point is theoretical (induction heads, Olsson et al. 2022), not tested.
  quote: "we argue that the near-perfect performance on Needle-in-the-Haystack may overestimate the long-context capabilities of LLMs"
  where: Sec 3.1, p.6
- The context style and the retrieval direction each change how hard the probe is.
  number: none
  setup: Document probe = bi-directional retrieval over natural language. Database probe = forward retrieval over structured data. Code probe = backward retrieval.
  quote: "both context styles and retrieval patterns significantly contribute to the hardness of the probing tasks."
  where: Sec 4.2, p.9
- IN2 training (synthetic long-context QA where the answer sits at random positions) largely removes the middle dip in the tested setting.
  number: Document Gap 32.1 → 6.1, Code Gap 59.5 → 18.7, Database Gap 77.0 → 16.8 (Mistral-v0.2 → FILM-7B). Avg 74.2 → 85.4, 20.3 → 83.3, 47.5 → 89.0.
  setup: Fine-tuning Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2. Data is 1.1M fine-grained QA (~63%), 300K multi-segment QA (~17%), 150K short QA (~9%), 200K OpenOrca instruction data (~11%). Contexts run 4K-32K tokens built from ~128-token C4 realnewslike segments. QA pairs were generated by GPT-4-Turbo. One epoch of ~14K steps, batch 128, peak LR 1e-6, ~300 GPU days (16 nodes x 8 A100 80G).
  quote: "FILM-7B has comparable performance with GPT-4-Turbo on the database probing task, and exhibits better robustness in document and code probing tasks."
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 1, p.6 and p.8. Training details are in Sec 2.1-2.2, pp.4-5.
- The gain transfers to real long-context tasks. The authors show only that the training helps; they do not show that the middle loss causes these tasks to fail.
  number: NarrativeQA F1 23.5 → 26.9; average over 9 LongBench tasks 30.6 → 39.9 (GPT-4-Turbo 44.7). HotpotQA 42.4 → 62.1. MuSiQue 20.8 → 39.0. MultiFQA 45.9 → 56.0.
  setup: 9 LongBench tasks. Inputs are middle-truncated to 32K. F1 for QA, ROUGE-L for summarization. Greedy decoding.
  quote: "FILM-7B (ours) 26.9 42.2 56.0 62.1 47.0 39.0 33.8 25.1 26.9 39.9"
  where: Table 2, p.7
  - Summarization is flat or worse: MultiNews 26.8 → 26.9 and QMSum 24.8 → 25.1, but GovReport 33.3 → 33.8. Mistral-v0.2's row ends "26.8 30.6" and FILM-7B's ends "26.9 39.9".
- Short-context ability is kept: MMLU 59.3 → 59.2.
  number: Figure 5, text-visible values only: MMLU 59.3 → 59.2. The other bar values are garbled in the extraction (see PROBLEMS).
  setup: 5-shot MMLU, 8-shot GSM8K, 4-shot MATH, 0-shot for the rest.
  quote: "maintaining a comparable performance on short-context tasks (e.g., 59.3→59.2 accuracy on MMLU)"
  where: Abstract, p.1
- A sliding-window attention model cannot retrieve beyond its window, and IN2 training does not fix that.
  number: 4K sliding window. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 (sliding window) scores Avg 44.8 on Document, 6.8 on Code and 8.8 on Database.
  setup: Experiments use 20% of the training data. Window applied in IN2 only or in both pre-training and IN2.
  quote: "the performances drop dramatically when the distance between the retrieval question and information is longer than the sliding window size."
  where: Sec 4.3, p.10, Fig 6
- A larger RoPE base θ helps IN2 training, so the authors suggest 10x the default.
  number: AllAvg 80.3 (1e6) → 83.8 (2e6) → 84.9 (1e7) → 84.6 (1e8); AllGap 23.6 → 16.5 → 14.3 → 14.0
  setup: FILM-7B trained on 20% of the data. Sec 4.3 states "We suggest to use a 10 times of the default RoPE base θ".
  quote: "1.0 × 107 83.7 7.6 81.7 18.4 89.4 16.8 84.9 14.3"
  where: Table 3, p.9

LIMITS
- This is a training fix for a 7B model, not something a prompt-side practitioner can apply. The paper gives no prompt or context-placement remedy.
- The root-cause explanation is a hypothesis. No ablation checks the position-bias story.
- The probes are retrieval-only and about 32K tokens. Each uses a single model per row and greedy decoding, with no variance or seeds reported.
- The model has a 32K window. The paper does not examine longer contexts or multi-needle placement, and it does not examine RAG-style distractors.
- The paper does not state an explicit limitations section.
- The paper does not run a separate test of position effects on real tasks.
- It dates from April 2024. The models it compares (Mistral-7B-v0.2, GPT-4-Turbo, LongAlign, InternLM2) are old, and nothing in it speaks to current frontier models.
- The paper does not compare against the original Liu et al. synthetic document-QA setup, which it cites.
- The Table 2 figures for models marked ∗ are copied from other papers, so they are not run under the same conditions.

BUILDS ON: Liu et al. 2024 and Xu et al. 2023 (lost-in-the-middle, as the paper cites them); Mohtashami & Jaggi 2024 (passkey retrieval); gkamradt Needle-in-the-Haystack (a GitHub repo); Olsson et al. 2022 (induction heads); Sun et al. 2021 and Sharan et al. 2018 (next-token loss depends on nearby tokens); Mistral 7B, Jiang et al. 2023; LongAlign, Bai et al. 2024; InternLM2, Cai et al. 2024; LongBench, Bai et al. 2023; RoPE-base context-extension work (Roziere et al. 2023; Xiong et al. 2023); RULER, Hsieh et al. 2024 (cited as related probing work); C4, Raffel et al. 2020; OpenOrca, Lian et al. 2023.

CODE: Training and data-generation templates only, no code.
- Training template, Appendix D Example 9, p.19: `[INST] Below is a context and an instruction. Based on the information provided in the context, write a response for the instruction. ### Context: Li ### Instruction: qi [/INST]` and the output is `ai`.
- Data equations, p.3-4: Eq. 1 `Li = ⊕{Shuffle(si, [rj])}` for one required segment, and Eq. 2 `Li = ⊕{Shuffle([si], [rj])}` for two or more.
- The multi-hop prompt (Example 8) says the question must require "at least two pieces".

FIGURES (captions only; I did not run the figures script)
- Fig 1, p.1: FILM-7B vs Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 vs GPT-4-Turbo on the three probes. It shows the dip in the middle of the context and the flatter FILM-7B curve.
- Fig 3, p.4: The three VAL probe formats (document sentence, code function name, database entity). This is the quickest way to see what forward, backward and bi-directional retrieval mean.
- Fig 4a-c, p.5: FILM-7B against Mistral, LongAlign and InternLM2 over position.
- Fig 6, p.9: Sliding-window runs, showing the cliff at the window size.
- Fig 7, p.18: FILM-7B near-perfect on NIAH.

PROBLEMS
- Figure curve data and the short-context bar values are not recoverable from the text extraction. Fig 5's numbers come out as a jumble ("59.3 85.4 46.0 70.0 55.9 83.6 40.4 8.7 59.2 87.7 ..."), so I only report MMLU 59.3 → 59.2, which the abstract confirms.
- The Table 1 header reads "Document Code Database AllAvg Gap ↓ Avg Gap ↓ ...". Each row has 8 numbers, which I read as three Avg/Gap pairs followed by the All pair. In the FILM-7B row 85.9 is the All-Avg and 13.9 is the All-Gap. The caller should check the column mapping against the PDF page before quoting a specific cell.
- The Gap figures are max-minus-min across positions, so they measure position variance rather than the specific middle-position drop. The paper does not report a middle-versus-edge number.
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
- The target note contained no "lost-in-the-middle" string, so claims were not matched to existing text.
